title: Days for a wound to heal
intro:
Illustrative data, made up for this book. In a study of a new dressing, 24 patients were followed until their wound healed, and every wound healed, so there is no censoring. Fit a Weibull model to the days to healing.

Give the fitted shape β and scale η (two decimals), and the probability that a wound is still not healed after 30 days, S(30) = P(T > 30) (four decimals).

In the Workbench: **Continuous distribution**, **Distribution** *Weibull*, **Parameters from** *Fitted to a data column*, the column of days, **Value of interest** 30.

MoreThan.says: That is P(T ≤ 30), the share healed by day 30. Survival is the share not yet healed: S(t) = P(T > t).

hints: The fit is item 5.6's maximum-likelihood Weibull fit.
